transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Jamie Lin (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Aegir CTO), Priya Rao (ML Eng Lead), Jordan Kim (Infra)
Links referenced: pricing deck (drive/redwood/pricing.pdf), security pack (drive/redwood/security.pdf), benchmark spreadsheet (sheets/aegir-bench)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on migration from OpenAI -> Redwood Dedicated. Aegir is evaluating cost parity, latency SLOs, and security (VPC/KMS). They run a mix of chat completions and embedding workloads; currently using OpenAI and experimenting with vLLM/TGI on-prem. Interested in pilot and parity benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and pain points
- Traffic profile and latency/cost targets
- Compatibility: model APIs, tokenizer, vLLM/TGI runtimes
- Security/compliance: VPC, KMS, SOC2, audit logs
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros - i'm alex, AE at Redwood, jamie is our se, we'll be mostly asking about your stack and what success looks like
[00:18] Samir: yeah thanks, i'm samir, cto at aegir, priya runs the ml stack, jordan is infra. we currently use open ai for prod gen, and we've got an on prem experiment with vllm for lower cost runs
[00:36] Jamie: great, can you give a quick breakdown of volume? tokens, calls per second, any p99 latency goals?
[00:45] Priya: sure, at peak we do about 120 rps across a few endpoints, avg request ~400 tokens, embeddings runs batch of ~2k docs daily. p95 latency target is 400 ms for the chat endpoint, p99 we'd like under 800 if possible
[01:05] Jordan: infra constraint is we can't expose customer PII to third party services; so VPC or private deployment is a must for some customers
[01:15] Alex: totally, that's common. do you have a preference between hosted/dedicated/private?
[01:22] Samir: prefer dedicated first — we want reserved capacity without full private ops overhead, but for some regulated customers we might need private later
[01:33] Jamie: understood. one common question is compatibility: are you using OpenAI API shapes, or custom wrappers?
[01:41] Priya: mostly openai-compatible shapes; we do some custom prompt templates. we also toyed with tgi/vllm for faster loops but integration is brittle — tokenizer and kvcache differences popped up
[02:00] Jamie: noted, on the Redwood Dedicated side we support OpenAI-style routes and also lower-level model endpoints. we do have an adapter for common tokenizers — sometimes tokens count differs a few tokens, so we recommend a small eval parity check
[02:17] Samir: that's important — we saw paraphrasing differences when switching from openai to a local llm, so eval parity is a blocker for product teams
[02:28] Alex: fair. we typically run a parity benchmark against your eval set and measure generation diffs + quality metrics. jamie, can you explain the parity approach?
[02:35] Jamie: yeah, so we take their prompt set, run it against the current provider and then against our dedicated instance. we compare rouge/bleu-ish style metrics plus manual spot checks for hallucinations; also measure latency/cost per token. we can automate with their existing harness if they share it
[02:55] Priya: perfect. about models — do you support the same families as openai? like major chat models?
[03:03] Jamie: we host a catalog of open models and also curated variants with quantization profiles. for many teams we match the behavior of the openai-family models closely, but exact parity depends on model weights; if you're running an openai proprietary model that's not available, we discuss fallbacks or hybrid routing to hosted for certain calls
[03:22] Samir: right now we use gpt-style endpoints from openai plus some smaller open models for non-critical tasks. we want to reduce cost without regressing on quality for customer-facing completions
[03:33] Jordan: also curious about throughput and autoscaling: can dedicated burst on extra capacity during peaks?
[03:40] Alex: yes, dedicated supports configurable burst pools and autoscaling policies. you get reserved baseline throughput and can configure burst/queueing behaviors. we can show simulated load curves in the pilot
[03:51] Priya: ok cool. security — KMS integration and audit logs are must-haves. do you allow customer-managed KMS?
[03:58] Jamie: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private; for Dedicated we offer KMS integration and key management options — we'll share the security pack with details (SOC2 + ISO pages)
[04:12] Samir: great. data residency? some of our EU clients require data to stay in eu-west region
[04:18] Alex: we can pin region routing and replicate logs to the region; for strict residency we'd recommend Private or a Dedicated pool in the region — we have EU regions live
[04:28] Priya: one ops question — how much engineering time to migrate? our infra team is small, we want minimal changes to the codebase
[04:35] Jamie: most customers integrate with our API as a drop-in for OpenAI-compatible calls — tokens and responses map closely. for embeddings we can provide a compatibility layer and migration scripts. we'll work with you on a small adapter to keep the app changes minimal
[04:52] Samir: the other thing, cost modeling. we've built an internal cost model showing openai is ~2.4x the cost per 1M tokens vs running on our on prem vllm. how do you help with cost decisioning?
[05:06] Alex: Redwood Optimize provides suggestions: batching, caching prefixes, quantization profiles. For Dedicated we can show estimated unit cost under different batch sizes and quant levels. if you have sample traffic we'll run a cost simulation for you
[05:21] Priya: is there an SDK change? we prefer not to rewrite our sdk layer — currently it's wrapped around openai python SDK
[05:27] Jamie: SDKs map to openai shapes in our client libs, so minimal change. we also provide native grpc endpoints if you prefer lower-latency paths for high throughput
[05:40] Jordan: curious about running vllm/tgi workloads on Redwood — can we keep those models and run them under the Redwood runtime?
[05:49] Jamie: we support loading TGI/vLLM-compatible checkpoints for many architectures. caveat: performance and kernel selection differ; we can help with quantization/compile profiles. sometimes small code changes are needed for kv cache handling, but we can consult on that in the technical deep-dive
[06:09] Samir: sounds good. about canarying — can we route a percentage of traffic to Redwood Dedicated and fall back to OpenAI if failures happen?
[06:18] Alex: yes, smart routing supports canary/gradual rollouts and automatic fallback to a different deployment or hosted provider if SLOs breach. you can set policies per route
[06:28] Priya: what about integration with our SSO and RBAC? we have SAML identity provider already
[06:33] Jamie: Redwood Console supports SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and role based access. we'll share the RBAC doc in the security pack
[06:42] Jordan: on observability — do you provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards?
[06:49] Alex: yep, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model dashboards, traces, and alerting. you can also push traces to your datadog or new relic if you want
[06:58] Priya: ok real quick — what does the pilot look like? we're thinking a 4-week pilot with 3x endpoints and a parity eval
[07:05] Alex: typical pilot is 3-6 weeks: setup Dedicated pool, load your eval suite, run parity & throughput benchmarks, iterate on quant/profile. we'll measure quality metrics and cost delta. jamie will own the bench tests
[07:18] Samir: good. what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[07:22] Alex: we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets on Dedicated with monitoring and incident response; details depend on contract tier — we'll include standard SLOs in the pricing doc
[07:33] Priya: any common gotchas when migrating from OpenAI?
[07:36] Jamie: a few: tokenizer mismatches (small token count diffs), randomness/seed differences leading to slight output divergence, and different default decode heuristics. all solvable with parity tuning and sometimes model variant choices
[07:50] Samir: ok that seems manageable. last, procurement — we'll need SOC2 + data processing agreement for legal
[07:57] Alex: understood, i'll attach the security pack and a draft DPA for legal to review
[08:04] Jordan: timeline — we want pilot in mid march and a production decision by end of april if things look good
[08:11] Alex: that's doable. we'll target pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-15 pending you sharing eval set and traffic profile
[08:18] Priya: we'll get that over by friday (notes: 2026-03-05)
[08:23] Alex: perfect. recap and next steps — i'll send pricing + security docs; jamie will run bench once we have the eval set; customer to share prompts and traffic; schedule deep-dive with infra
[08:35] Samir: thanks everyone
[08:37] Alex: thanks, talk soon

End of transcript.
